analysis: The PR is documentation only: docs/reference/configuration.md gains two rows at head lines ~401-402 documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY, which are default-on negative-disable MTP scheduling toggles. The row text says they are not forwarded to LaunchAgents. The supplied units are a base excerpt (lines 520-687) and a head excerpt (lines 1-353), so the changed head lines 401-402 are only visible in the patch excerpt, which is also truncated. I could not cite them as visible head lines, and I found no source change. The documented behavior covers Qwen inline-MTP decode scheduling and hidden-state carry, which is performance scheduling inside TB-007. It does not touch the coordinator wire contract (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009, TB-011), key custody, or the prefix cache (T-041). No new network surface, secret handling, environment passthrough or cache storage behavior is described. The remaining text in the supplied units is unchanged context, for example the SSD prefix cache table and the media budgets. I checked that it is consistent with T-041 on the 1800 s TTL cap, the KEK handling and the debug-key-file restrictions. The unverified contract is that the underlying library code (MTPContractsV2.swift) matches the docs, for example that the carry or chained-decode paths do not alter request isolation or per-request KV state. That code is not in the supplied evidence, so I record it as an integration question and not as a finding. No finding is raised.
